text: TCP delivers bytes reliably and in order. Why does a receiver still need framing?
choices: TCP silently drops packets over 1500 bytes, so long messages must be split by the sender.
TCP gives a stream of bytes, not messages — ten writes may arrive as one read, or one write as three.
TCP may reorder messages under congestion, so a sequence number is required.
TCP does not guarantee delivery, so each message needs an application-level acknowledgement.
explanation: There is no `readMessage`, because TCP does not know what a message is. The three answers are a delimiter, a length prefix, or closing the connection. Omitting framing produces a program that works on localhost — which happens to deliver each write as one read — and fails over a real network, which is the classic symptom.
